newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE might seek arbitration over Italy rocket row.
newsitem.headline: UAE might seek arbitration over Italy rocket row.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates would seek international arbitration if talks with Italian officials failed to settle a row with Italy's BPD Difesa e Spazio (Fiat Avio Group) over rocket launchers, an official said.

"We asked the company to look into the issue but no solution was reached. There are presently discussions at the Italian government level to find a solution which satisfies both sides," said Lieutenant-General Sheikh Mohammad bin Zaid al-Nahayan, Chief of Staff of the UAE armed forces.

"But, if such a solution is not reached (the UAE) will take the issue to international arbitration in Swiss courts," he said in an interview with the English-language Gulf News daily published on Wednesday.
The UAE said in March it had decided to halt military deals with Italian firms due to the row with BPD, running since 1994.
The UAE, a prized player in the international arms market, withdrew the Italian-made rapid launcher rocket system from military use in 1996 due to a recurring technical malfunction.
The 24 multiple-launchers and thousands of surface-to-surface rockets, with a 30-km (19-mile) range, were bought in the 1980s for $280 million. The problem did not appear until 1994.
